I saw a few reviews for this game and it was a little depressing to see some negative reviews for such a great game.

First off, while the story isnt the greatest thing, it still tells a 'compelling' story while you try to find what happened to 'Bit' (the hacker that had a deadmans switch which you read at the start of the game).

The hacking is extremely fun, yet simple and makes you feel extremely powerful, which is what games like this SHOULD do. Nobody wants to sit down and just be a code junkie. Everyone wants to feel like they can destroy anything they touch, and this game does it masterfully.

Some negative reviews I read said that "the game is too simple because if you want to hack an ssh port you just run SSHCrack.exe etc., and I get the annoyance behind that, but they also forget to talk about the trace mechanic behind it. While you are probing a computer and opening ports, you are usually being traced, and a couple times I had barely any time remaining to finish porthacking to log in before I could start tracekill.exe. It keeps you on your toes and makes you figure out what ports are faster to open depending on how many need to be opened. The DLC also adds more hacking tools which adds a bit more depth to the entire port hacking.

One negative thing I did notice was that logs never seemed to matter, as some negative reviews have stated. I find that a little upsetting that it must not actually mean anything because its now second nature to me to just type rm * /log whenever I do anything on a server.

And the soundtrack? The soundtrack is great. Everyones notable song is the final battle song where you hack a server and delete tons of files, which plays Roller Mobster by Carpenter Brut (everyones favorite Hotline Miami 2 song). The DLC also has some great music in it as well and it adds to the experience tenfold.

I also got to speak to the creator over on twitter and he seemed like a genuinely great guy and that he is excited to be working on more projects. Now that he's on my radar I'll definitely be keeping an eye out for his newer games and (hopefully) more DLC for hacknet now that this game is getting massive success from being F2P for a short time.

Definitely buy/download the game and give it a shot. It seems like a lot to take in at first, but after you get the hang of it, the game is extremely enjoyable..

Hacknet... I don't even know where to start with this game.

Hacknet is not your average game. Some games may be incredibly immersive, like FPSes and VR games. Hacknet is not designed to be like this.

In most cases, Hacknet is also not an intense game. You aren't tested on your reaction time or click speed. You are tested, instead, on your abilities to adapt to different environments and solve problems as they pop up in your face.

Hacknet is also not what I'd consider a Christian game. Although there are few swear words to be found in the game (minus the IRC logs), Hacknet's plot involves learning to be a hacker using a simplistic set of Unix-inspired tools and a combination of a GUI and terminal environment.

When you start the game, you may not be incredibly impressed with the low amount of character development, as the basis of the game is just learning to use your environment, but you will eventually learn that a repetitive element of the game becomes a major part of the plot.

Even as shown by the creator's development timelapse (available to view at the end of the game), this game is not incredibly complex, but hours upon hours of work have been put into it and the average gamer will gain hours of fun.

To summarize the game as a whole, Hacknet is about diving into a world that is not your own and helping to fulfill an uncannily skilled hacker's death wishes. You learn to take advantage of a user environment known as the Hacknet OS and join several virtual hacker groups in an attempt to follow breadcrumbs left behind by Bit.

The soundtrack is co-written by several somewhat popular artists. It is dynamic to your actions in the game, having more intense music being played in more intense missions, and likewise for calmer, more reflective portions of the game. (If you loved the soundtrack as much as I did, please be sure to purchase it as DLC. It's available in the game folder after purchasing and downloading. My favorite tracks are Broken Boy and Bit.)

I am not a game critic, simply a lowly gamer. But the impact this game has had on my life is incredible. The plot is masterfully crafted and better than any movie I've ever watched. The graphics, although simple, are fancy enough to fit the experience (although epileptic persons may want to avoid the end of the game). As I have described, the soundtrack is amazing. Everything about this game makes it worth at least a couple hours away from Fortnite.

Having sat through the entire game in one sitting, I can definitely reccomend playing the game to anyone who's into classic command line style games, althought it does require a tiny bit of technical knowhow, such as what directories are, what commands need in order to run (In a [Program Name] [Port Number/File Name] [Password] format), and memorising at least 8 or 9 commands you'll be using frequently throughout mid to end game. 

This would be fine if the commands were one word bt the majority of them consist of 1-3 words and may or may not have an underscore, making simple things like uploading files with long names a chore.

I think it's definitely doable if you've got some dexterity and typing speed, as you're required to do a lot in the space of 30 seconds. 

Pros:
- It's got a good story behind the scenes, and rewards you for going out of your way to find bits and pieces, looking in places you shouldn't, etc.
- The game itself doesn't take up a lot of space, and doesn't require a good computer to run.
- It teaches you a lot about the "society" around hacking, giving off a more "for the people" mindset that really makes you think about the ethics of hacking
- It has an inbuilt clicker game for free. (Which you can also hack like literally everything else)
- There's a dedicated wiki and fanbase around the game already, making searching for help that much more easier for new players.
- You're rewarded for playing the game a second time, with some extra content (though you may have already found it without the hint given to you), giving it some replayability rather than a "play it once and put it down" game.

Cons:
- It's repetitive, there's no getting around it for a text based game, however some long winded file names make it much worse, there is a shortcut where you press tab and it autocompletes, but 6 times out of 10 it just doesn't work.
- There isn't a lot of customisability until much later on in the game.
- There's a site in the game that literally rips off the 4chan format, although I admit the colour scheme is kinda cool.
- The tutorial doesn't tell you about commands that are pretty essential to the gameplay, I had to use guides to figure some bits out.

Overall, I'd give it a solid 8/10.

Hacknet is a simulator situated really close to real hacking - true, but it's also something way bigger. It's an epic story. A possibility for a player to enforce the type of gameplay he desires. Yes - you can cooperate with a hacking group but in the meantime you can hack their server and read their personal e-mails. 

Don't get me wrong - this game is linear. You can't get to other endings. You can't make other people react to your actions. Even when you intentionally send a guy p.e: wrong password - he won't respond. Only "Mission incompleted" window will pop up. It's not even like the player thinks he can make the world respond - you don't have any illusion of sandbox. 

Still tough. The Game left me thinking. Not about the story of Bit. Not about the story of V. Not even about the genius of the maker, nooo... I was thinking: "What the hell am I going to do with my life now?". I am amazed. I am mesmerized. I approve. Brown, out!
